en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, the national bird, inhabits the tropical forests of Mindanao and eastern Luzon.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines and provides a major source of hydroelectric power for the region.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of exactly 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its pristine coral biodiversity.
The northeast monsoon, locally called amihan, brings cool and dry air to the Philippines from November to February every year.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are ancient agricultural landmarks carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
The Philippines is the top global producer of abaca, a tropical banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make ropes.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry summer season.
The Visayas is a central island group in the Philippines comprising major islands like Panay, Negros, Cebu, Bohol, and Leyte.
Surigao del Norte in Mindanao contains some of the largest known nickel reserves in the world, supporting a major mining industry.
